nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{Q}^d$ and a natural number $m$, the ordinary Ehrhart count is the number $|mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$ of integer points in the dilate $mP = \{m x : x \in P\}$, where $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is viewed inside $\mathbb{Q}^d$; it is $0$ when $mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ is infinite.
